subject: Post-demo: QuikMart hosting recommendation — latency vs throughput
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Aurelia Gomez <aurelia@quikmart.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: QuikMart hosting recommendation — latency vs throughput

Aurelia — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and our recommended path so we can align on next steps. I kept the notes focused on the hosting trade-offs you asked about: Hosted API vs Dedicated reserved capacity vs Private VPC/on-prem.

Recap of what you said on the call:
- Production baseline: ~350 QPS sustained during business hours, peaks to ~2k QPS for checkout flows.
- Current p95 service latency target: aiming for <=90ms for the new real-time personalization call. Today’s CPU infra is ~120ms p95.
- Compliance note: payment card interactions touch tokenized identifiers; you flagged that security review will be required.

High-level recommendation (short):
- Pilot: run on Hosted API for 2–4 weeks if you can tolerate a pilot p95 up to ~150ms while we validate traffic and kernels. Hosted gets you fastest time to value.
- Production: if the p95 requirement is <=100ms at sustained 350 QPS (and bursts to 2k), we recommend Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) with autoscale + burst. Dedicated gives predictable tail latency and isolation for model hotspots.
- Private VPC/on-prem: consider only if your compliance or data residency rules mandate it; it adds time and a separate support path.

Why Dedicated for strict p95 and sustained QPS:
- Dedicated lets us pin model variant + quantization and tune batching without noisy-neighbor effects.
- Autoscale and burst pools handle 2k spikes while preserving low tail latency.

Requested from you (action items):
1) Can you share a 48–72 hour sample of real traffic (ideally a CSV with timestamp, request size, user bucket) so our infra team can microbenchmark?
2) Confirm whether the p95 target is hard <=90ms or a phased goal (e.g., 90ms for checkout only).
3) Who owns procurement? we’ll send a small pilot SOW/PO to stop-gap capacity if you choose Dedicated for pilot.

Attachments: quikmart-pilot-plan.xlsx (pilot scope & SOW draft), latency-qps-benchmarks.pdf (sample Redwood internal numbers for similar profiles).

Next internal touch: Ben and Neha — can you prep a quick Dedicated sizing note and a Hosted fallback plan for the pilot so we can share a crisp choose-1/2-path?

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Sr. Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
viv@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Post-demo: QuikMart hosting recommendation — latency vs throughput

Vivek — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 
- The 350 QPS number is our daytime average over the catalog recommendation endpoint. Checkout/real-time personalization can spike to ~2k for flash promotions.
- The 90ms p95 is our product target for checkout personalization specifically; we could accept up to 120ms for non-checkout profile calls.
- On compliance: we need SOC 2 Type II evidence and details on log retention and encryption. We may need VPC isolation if the security review flags the payment flow.

SRE note (from SRE team): our logs retention policy requires audit logs for 12 months and we must maintain control-plane auditability. If Dedicated can run in a VPC with customer-managed KMS, that would cover most of our requirements.

Procurement: I’m copying finance here — procurement will need an estimate for a 3-month pilot and an expected monthly committed price for Dedicated.

Next asks: 
- Can Redwood provide a dedicated sizing sketch (vCPU/GPU counts, estimated sustained cost) for achieving <=90ms p95 at 350 sustained QPS and with 2x headroom for safety?
- Can you confirm whether a hybrid approach (Hosted for non-critical calls + Dedicated for checkout) is supported with automatic routing/fallback?

Aurelia Gomez
Head of Product, QuikMart
aurelia@quikmart.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 02:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: QuikMart hosting recommendation — latency vs throughput (internal)

Team — quick sizing draft based on Aurelia’s numbers. This is internal and meant to be a starting point for the pilot SOW.

Assumptions from call:
- Sustained production: 350 QPS
- Target p95: <=90ms for checkout calls
- Peak burst: 2k QPS (short duration)

Sizing sketch (recommended):
- Dedicated reserved pool: 4 nodes (each node: 8xA100-equivalent inference slots) with autoscale up to 8 nodes for bursts. This gives headroom for model KV cache and batch ceilings to keep p95 in target for the checkout path.
- Pilot fallback: run checkout calls on Dedicated; route other calls to Hosted API with routing policy and rate-limited fallback. This reduces initial reserve cost while we validate behavior.
- Security: propose Dedicated in customer VPC mode with customer-managed KMS for keys and audit log export to their SIEM. If QuikMart requires full on-prem, that’s a separate timeline.

Estimated ballpark (for procurement): monthly committed = "$XXk" for reserved baseline (4-node pool) + overage/burst charges. Ben — can you convert to a clean procurement line item and a 90-day pilot PO draft?

Action items:
- Ben: pilot PO draft + line items for 4-node baseline + burst buffer.
- Vivek: coordinate technical deep dive with QuikMart SRE to validate network/KMS requirements.
- Marissa: prepare a short one-page talk track for the customer success & finance folks to smooth procurement.

-Neha

Aurelia — appreciate the detail. We’re aligned on next steps; below is a short, concrete plan so Procurement and SRE have what they need.

Immediate next steps (this week):
1) You: share 48–72 hour traffic sample (CSV) and confirm which endpoints must hit <=90ms p95.
2) Redwood: Ben will send a 90-day pilot PO draft and pricing sketch for a 4-node Dedicated baseline + burst buffer (ballpark by EOD Thursday).
3) Redwood infra: Neha and I will run microbenchmarks against the sample dataset and return a p95 projection for Hosted vs Dedicated.
4) Security: I’ll attach our security pack and SOC2 pointer; if you want, we can schedule a short call with our security lead next Tuesday to walk through VPC/KMS options.

Routing/fallback note: yes — we support a hybrid model. You can route checkout traffic to Dedicated and keep non-critical calls on Hosted. Automatic fallback policies exist (route to Hosted if Dedicated capacity is exhausted) but we’ll want to agree on SLOs and throttling behaviors in the pilot.

Deliverables we’ll share: pilot SOW, Dedicated sizing sketch, microbenchmark report, security pack (SOC2 summary + KMS options).

If this looks good, I’ll loop in our security lead and schedule the SRE deep dive for next Tue/Wed.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this forward.

Vivek Kulkarni
